name: EU API Latency Degradation
description: EU customers are reporting slow project loading times. Latency has increased significantly for EU-region API calls, while US and AP regions are unaffected.

root_cause.summary: N+1 query bug in ProjectService.getProjectsForUser() — calls GdprDataFilter.filterProject() per project in a loop instead of using the batch filterProjects() method. Each call executes a separate SQL query against gdpr_audit_log table.
root_cause.mechanism: The for loop at line 50 iterates over all projects and calls gdprDataFilter.filterProject(project) at line 51, which triggers checkComplianceStatus() at GdprDataFilter.java:73, executing an individual SQL query per project. A user with 50 projects generates 50 extra DB queries per request. The batch method filterProjects() at GdprDataFilter.java:53 exists and uses a single IN query but is not called.
root_cause.trigger: Deployment v2.3.1 of project-service at 2024-01-15T13:45:00Z introduced this code path. It only affects EU regions because the N+1 loop is inside an if-block checking EU_REGIONS at ProjectService.java:47.
root_cause.why_not_caught: Dev/staging has <5 projects per user, so the N+1 pattern was invisible. Production EU enterprise customers have 50-200 projects per user.

red_herring.description: Redis config change deployed to redis-cache at 2024-01-15T12:30:00Z — updated maxmemory-policy from 'allkeys-lru' to 'volatile-lru'. This deployment shows up in timeline but is unrelated to the latency issue. Redis metrics are healthy.

args.title: EU API latency degradation — N+1 query in GDPR filter
